what_it_does: Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) — the technique of computing on data that stays encrypted throughout — is extraordinarily computationally expensive, orders of magnitude slower than ordinary computation. The core expensive operation is called key-switching: it refreshes the encryption keys that get worn down after each arithmetic step. FAST is a dedicated chip that speeds up key-switching by adopting two recently developed cryptographic optimizations: 'hoisting' (which reuses partial results across multiple key-switching operations instead of recomputing them) and the KLSS method (a different algebraic decomposition of the key that requires fewer and cheaper operations). Because different parts of an FHE computation need different levels of numerical precision, FAST can dynamically adjust its arithmetic precision to match the current workload, avoiding wasted energy on unnecessarily high-precision arithmetic.
